title: August and the Tide
premise: Lena Quintana built her career orchestrating other people's perfect days while quietly nursing the wound of a wedding that never happened—hers, eleven years ago, on a coastal island where she left without explanation. When a renovation crew at the island's old inn uncovers an unsent letter from August Hale, the man she abandoned, Lena takes a job planning a society wedding there, telling herself it's business. But August never left; he runs the ferry and the inn now, and the letter reveals he waited for her. As the season's last ferry approaches, Lena must choose between the safe, fragmented life she's built and risking everything for a love that never stopped counting tides.
about_author: Lior Reyes spent three summers working hospitality on a small island ferry route, collecting stories from passengers who came back year after year. They write love stories about people who mistake timing for fate.

chapters.title: The Unsent Letter
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A contractor emails Lena a photo of a water-stained letter found in the walls of the Merrow Inn, postmarked eleven years ago, addressed to her in handwriting she'd know anywhere. She tells herself to throw it away but reads it twice instead. Emotional beat: old grief cracking open under new light.

chapters.title: Pieces Before the Whole
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Flashback-tinged scenes of Lena's meticulous life: a thriving planning business, a boyfriend who just proposed politely, a calendar with no gaps. Her sister Marisol accuses her of 'lending pieces' of herself to everyone. Emotional beat: the hollowness beneath competence.

chapters.title: The Calloway Wedding
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A high-profile client insists on the Merrow Inn on Bellhaven Island—the only venue available in September. Lena accepts, rationalizing that August probably sold the place years ago. Emotional beat: self-deception dressed as professionalism.

chapters.title: Last Ferry Out
chapters.summary: August's POV. August pilots the evening ferry, watching tourists thin out as summer ends. He's built a quiet life: the inn, his daughter Wren, the tide charts. When he sees Lena's name on the wedding contract, his hands go still on the wheel. Emotional beat: dread braided with hope.

chapters.title: Arrival
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The ferry docks and August is there, older, bearded, unreadable. Their exchange is all logistics and clipped courtesy while eleven years hum underneath. Wren, twelve and sharp-eyed, watches Lena like a puzzle. Emotional beat: the shock of the past made flesh.

chapters.title: What the Walls Kept
chapters.summary: August's POV. August confronts the letter's discovery privately, remembering writing it the night after Lena vanished—words he never mailed because he couldn't find her. He decides not to tell her yet. Emotional beat: protective silence as both kindness and cowardice.

chapters.title: Site Walk
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Walking the grounds with August, they fall into old rhythms—arguing about hydrangeas, finishing each other's vendor lists—then catch themselves. Lena learns he has a daughter and feels the floor tilt. Emotional beat: intimacy rekindling against her will.

chapters.title: Wren's Questions
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds Lena's old photograph tucked in a guest-room Bible and starts investigating, delighted by gossip potential. She quizzes her father, who deflects badly. Emotional beat: a child's clear sight cutting through adult fog.

chapters.title: Rain Check
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A storm strands the site-walk party indoors; power fails, candles come out. August and Lena talk until 2 a.m.—everything except the letter and why she left. She almost explains, then doesn't. Emotional beat: closeness that hurts more than distance.

chapters.title: The Fiancé Visits
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Daniel arrives unannounced with flowers and a venue-change offer. Seeing him beside August, Lena realizes she's been choosing safe over true for a decade. She sends Daniel home with the ring unanswered. Emotional beat: first honest crack in her constructed life.

chapters.title: Tide Charts
chapters.summary: August's POV. August teaches Wren to read the tide tables, a ritual he once planned to share with Lena. Wren asks point-blank if Lena is 'the one from the story.' August admits there was a story. Emotional beat: fatherhood forcing honesty.

chapters.title: Marisol's Verdict
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Marisol visits, clocks everything in one dinner, and delivers the truth: Lena didn't leave because of duty to her dying mother—she left because she was terrified of being fully known. Lena throws her out, then cries in the boathouse. Emotional beat: rage before reckoning.

chapters.title: The Letter Surfaces
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The contractor mails Lena the original letter. Reading it in full, she learns August waited at the dock three days after she left, that he wrote 'I will keep the porch light on.' She realizes he never stopped. Emotional beat: devastation and unbearable tenderness.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Dock
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Lena confronts August: why keep the letter secret? He counters: why leave without a word? Eleven years of hurt collide on the dock in front of the wedding crew. She finally confesses her mother's death, her panic, her shame. Emotional beat: the wound laid open together.

chapters.title: Cold Front
chapters.summary: August's POV. August retreats into work, telling himself some doors stay shut. Wren, furious at his stubbornness, sabotages by inviting Lena to dinner. The dinner is stiff, then real, then almost warm—until August cuts it short. Emotional beat: pride as armor cracking.

chapters.title: Wedding Eve Crisis
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The caterer cancels, a gale is forecast, and the bride threatens to elope. Lena holds the day together through sheer nerve while August quietly reroutes supplies on his ferry. Working side by side through the night, they rebuild something wordless between them. Emotional beat: partnership rediscovered under pressure.

chapters.title: Someone Else's Vows
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The Calloway wedding unfolds beautifully in a break in the weather. Watching the vows, Lena understands what she threw away—not a wedding, but a witness, someone who stays. August catches her crying and doesn't look away. Emotional beat: clarity arriving through borrowed joy.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: August's POV. October closes the tourist run. August stands at the dock with the season's final departure boarding—and makes his choice, holding the ferry for one passenger walking fast down the road. Emotional beat: the grand gesture inverted—he waits, she comes.

chapters.title: Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. On the empty ferry crossing, Lena gives August the whole truth and the whole heart—no pieces, no exits. He gives her the original letter, kept eleven years in a tin box. They arrive at the island as the sun sets, hands clasped. Emotional beat: surrender without losing self.

chapters.title: Porch Light
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren narrates the small domestic miracle: Lena's suitcase in the hall, three mugs at breakfast, her father humming. Wren claims credit for everything and begins teaching Lena the tide tables. Emotional beat: found family assembling itself.

chapters.title: Second Chances, Better Timing
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Spring: Lena splits her business between the city and the island, planning weddings only for couples who make her believe. On the rebuilt inn porch, August proposes with the same ring from eleven years ago, kept in the tin box. She says yes before he finishes. Emotional beat: joy earned, not granted.

chapters.title: August and the Tide
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POVs. One year later: their small wedding on the dock, guests including Marisol, Daniel (gracious now), and every islander who watched them circle each other. Wren signs the register as witness. The last line echoes the letter: the porch light stays on. Emotional beat: memory transformed from wound to foundation.
